reason: README Quickstart shows Python CustomVoice inference with a 0.6B public model that can run on CPU in float32.
demo: README Quickstart > Python Package Usage > Custom Voice Generate, using Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-CustomVoice on CPU
goal: Install the qwen-tts package from the repo and get Qwen3TTSModel.from_pretrained('Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-CustomVoice') running on CPU (device_map='cpu', dtype=torch.float32, no flash_attention). Then call generate_custom_voice with an English text, language='English', speaker='Ryan', and write the result to a wav file with soundfile. The wav must contain real synthesized speech.
check: The hidden test runs a short English CustomVoice synthesis on CPU and verifies a valid, non-silent speech wav of plausible duration is written.

revision.by: second review (outside the maintained set; independent log check of maintained passes)
issues: Vacuous assertion: `assert "Ryan" in [...] or True` can never fail (dead check). v2 asserts 'ryan' is in get_supported_speakers(), which returns a lowercased list (qwen3_tts_model.py:842-854).

Lenient on a broken model: with max_new_tokens=400 (~33 s at 12 Hz) and the duration cap at 60 s, a model that never emits end-of-speech and outputs noise passes the energy checks. v2 caps the duration at 20 s for this 10-word sentence (runs saw 6.9 s and 4.2 s).
evidence: src/qwenlm-qwen3-tts/qwen_tts/inference/qwen3_tts_model.py:165-185 - generate_custom_voice validates speakers case-insensitively; :842-854 get_supported_speakers returns sorted lowercase names

src/qwenlm-qwen3-tts/README.md:150-196 - CustomVoice snippet (cuda/bf16/flash-attn) and speaker table including Ryan; the goal's CPU/fp32/no-flash-attn adaptation is forced by the no-GPU sandbox and is not an install hint
